message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights & Protections | |------|--------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• Must comply with all local health and building codes. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • Landlord must repair major defects; tenant may pay for repairs and deduct from rent if landlord fails to act within a reasonable time. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) unless it’s an emergency. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for leases longer than one year.
• Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions (e.g., banning pets unless justified). | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must be in writing and not violate any local ordinances. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must give written notice (30 days for nonpayment, 60 days for lease violations).
• Eviction requires court action; landlord cannot forcibly remove tenant. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Property Code §92.001‑92.004 (race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, etc.). | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide water, heat, and electricity unless otherwise specified. | | **Insurance** | • Tenants are not required to carry renters insurance, but it’s highly recommended. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Landlord may prohibit subletting, but must do so in writing and cannot arbitrarily deny requests. | | **Notice of Lease Termination** | • For month-to-month leases, either party must give **30 days’ written notice**. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Tenants can sue for damages, recover unpaid rent, or seek injunctions if landlord violates lease or law. | #### Quick Tips for Tenants 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of lease, receipts, and communication with landlord. 2. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities have additional tenant protections (e.g., rent control, eviction moratoriums). 3. **Use the Texas Attorney General’s “Tenant’s Guide”** – A free resource with detailed rights and responsibilities. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or discrimination, contact a local legal aid organization or the Texas Legal Services Center. --- **Disclaimer:** This overview is for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice. Laws can change, and local ordinances may add additional protections. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney in Texas.
